question: Can a compiled annotation inventory and explicit finite invocation-count contract preserve required-test execution across source layouts?

codec.stage: frozen source-exposed transfer, not unseen validation

qualification: Compile original and each layout with javac --release 8 -g:none. Require byte-for-byte equal emitted test classfile maps within each candidate role before admitting a layout. Production fixed. Classfiles carry no debug tables in this new study. This does not retroactively alter earlier experiments.
candidate_origin: Both incorrect candidates are authored. No saved agent output is manufactured.
counts: Finite fixture invocation counts are independently frozen. General dynamic providers with unknown counts cannot receive a complete contract verdict.
negative_controls: Unchanged developer candidates must pass after complete execution; unannotated helper methods must not enter the compiled test inventory.
transfer: Implementation and layouts frozen before execution. Codec is already source-exposed; this is not a blind held-out case.
scope: Matched changed-method inventory is externally fixed, not end-to-end diff extraction or full benchmark regrade. Native JUnit Jupiter only.
execution_bound: Two sequential one-CPU one-GiB Azure jobs, at most one evidenced operational retry per case. Each child has a 275-second cap and 438-second cleanup deadline. Stop rather than adapt scientific hypotheses to outcomes.
source_packaging: Complete retained Java sources and pom files. Unrelated test resource fixtures omitted, including upstream local TLS test keys. Selected tests do not consume these resources.
